The Five Pillars of Islam. The foundational religious obligations for all Muslims have been codified in Islamic theology and law, forming the structural and ethical backbone of Islamic practice and belief. They bind the faith community through shared ritual and commitment, and performing the five pillars is essential to a Muslim's spiritual standing and forms the minimum required observance of the faith.

The Shahada is the testimony of faith, the declaration: There is no god but Allah, and Muhammad is his prophet. This is the central doctrinal statement that defines Islamic monotheism. Salat is mandatory ritual prayer five times daily at dawn, midday, afternoon, sunset, and night, performed facing Mecca individually or communally. Zakat is almsgiving, an obligatory tax on wealth and income typically two point five percent of accumulated savings, given to the poor and needy to purify one's earnings. Sawm is fasting, abstaining from food, drink, and other bodily needs during daylight hours throughout the month of Ramadan, Islam's holiest month. Hajj is the pilgrimage, the sacred journey to Mecca required once in a lifetime for all able-bodied and financially able Muslims, performed during the annual pilgrimage season.
